candidates: static/app/views/performance/newTraceDetails/traceDrawer/details/span/eapSections/attributes.tsx:65 - Hidden attributes are only filtered out when a search query is present.. `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` is only checked inside the `sorted.filter(...)` call. That call runs only when `searchQuery.trim()` is non-empty. In the default state with an empty search box, the early `return sorted;` returns every attribute. So `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` still show in the normal view, and the hiding only works while the user is searching. Fix: filter hidden attributes before the early return, e.g. `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`, then apply the search filter.

static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx:164 - With the feature flag on, every table widget renders as an empty table.. When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` gets hard-coded `columns={[]}` and empty `data`/`meta`, and `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields` and `loading` are all ignored. Any organization with the flag sees blank table widgets instead of its query results. Pass the real columns and table data built from `result` and `fields`, or keep the flag off until that is wired up.

src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:107 - Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` assumes nodestore returns every id, in request order.. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. Some backends and cache paths leave out ids that were not found, and the dict order is not guaranteed to match the request. If even one error is missing (expired or deleted), `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairs ids with the wrong payloads, so errors are labelled with other errors' ids and the last ones are dropped. Fix: iterate the ids directly, e.g. `for eid, nid in zip(error_ids, node_ids): data = events.get(nid)`.

src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:153 - Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with breadcrumb timestamps (milliseconds), so errors end up in the wrong place.. The `timestamp` from a nodestore event is a float in epoch seconds. Replay recording events carry `timestamp` in epoch milliseconds. Because `error_ts < event.get("timestamp", 0)` holds for every real event, all errors are emitted before the first breadcrumb, and the summary request loses the chronological order this merge sets out to build. The log line also prints the raw seconds value, while the breadcrumb messages use a different scale. Fix: convert the error timestamp to milliseconds (`* 1000`) when you build `ErrorEvent`, or normalise both sides before comparing.
